record.title: fix: query the entitlement whose contract scope is still live

notes: internal/proxy/dataworks_entitlement_selection_test.go:96 the new proxy test genuinely fails on pre-change code: ent_z_pilot is upserted last and sorts first (newer updated_at, and 'ent_z_pilot' > 'ent_a_live' on the id tiebreak), so old FindAPIEntitlement would have selected the dead-contract grant and returned 403 instead of the asserted 200/ent_a_live. The store test exercises the new ListAPIEntitlementCandidates directly. Both assert real values, not tautologies.

internal/proxy/dataworks_runtime.go:71 no authorization bypass: usableEntitlement is only a pre-filter, and every check it applies (entitlementActive, entitlementAllowsQuery, contract found + ProductKey match, contractScopeActive, sensitive purpose) is re-run on the selected row by the main handler at lines 74-126, plus rate limit and allowed_fields. Selection performs no writes and does not touch the rate limiter, matching the docs claim.

internal/store/dataworks_operations.go:497 sort.SliceStable's less function is a valid strict weak ordering (entitlementNewer falls back to string compare then id, so it is total and antisymmetric); FindAPIEntitlement returning ents[0] is behaviourally identical to the old active-first/newest logic it replaced.

internal/proxy/dataworks_runtime.go:219 stale comment: 'It delegates to the store so the row FindAPIEntitlement picks for a key is judged by the same rule that selected it.' The runtime no longer calls FindAPIEntitlement; after this change FindAPIEntitlement has no production caller at all (only internal/store/dataworks_entitlement_select_test.go). Harmless but worth cleaning up in a follow-up.

internal/proxy/dataworks_runtime.go:246 semantic change operators should know about: previously the newest active entitlement row won outright, so adding a new narrower row effectively narrowed access. Now an older active row with a permissive scope and a live contract still grants access, so narrowing/revoking must set status on every row for the key+product, not just add a newer one. docs/OPERATIONS.md:159 describes the new walk but does not spell out this revocation implication.

internal/proxy/dataworks_runtime.go:252 usableEntitlement swallows the GetContractScope error (err != nil is treated the same as 'not found' and the candidate is skipped). If all candidates error the handler falls back to candidates[0] and re-queries at line 100, surfacing a 500, so no error is lost silently; but a transient failure on one candidate can quietly shift which grant is billed via IncrementUsageMetering.

internal/store/dataworks_operations.go:479 worst case is now up to 50 extra GetContractScope round-trips per query request (LIMIT 50 candidates x one lookup each). Fine for the documented 'handful of rows per product', but it is an N+1 that scales with entitlement count.
docs/OPERATIONS.md:161 the fallback error list omits scope_denied, which the handler can still return at line 80 when candidates[0] is active but its scope disallows query. Minor doc gap only.
Working tree has an uncommitted deletion of web/dist/.gitkeep. It is not part of git diff main...HEAD, so it is pre-existing dirt rather than this change, but it should not be swept into the merge.

go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... -count=1 all pass clean on this branch. No migrations, no external state changes, no dependency or formatting churn; the change is a pure code revert away.
